0|151f0ec9ddb539c403a17c86da092e751736c121|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"scsi: scsi_debug: Drop sdebug_dev_info.num_in_q
In schedule_resp()
column2: under certain conditions we check whether the

column1: per-device queue is full (num_in_q == queue depth - 1) and we may inject a
task set full"" (TSF) error if it is.
However how we read num_in_q is racy - many threads may see the same ""queue
is full"" value (and also issue a TSF).
There is per-queue locking in reading per-device num_in_q
not help.
Replace how we read num_in_q at this location with a call to
scsi_device_busy(). Calling scsi_device_busy() is likewise racy (as reading
num_in_q)
column2: so nothing lost or gained. Calling scsi_device_busy() is also

column1: slow as it needs to read all bits in the per-device budget bitmap
can live with that since we're just a simulator and it's only under a
certain configs which we would see this.
Also move the ""task set full"" print earlier as it would only be called now
under this condition. However
column2: previously it may not have been called -

column1: like returning early - but keep it simple and always call it.
At this point we can drop sdebug_dev_info.num_in_q - it is difficult to
maintain properly and adds extra normal case command processing.
